title: Medical Child Abuse from an Interprofessional Perspective: An Exploratory Survey Study on Knowledge, Perceptions, Action Confidence, and Barriers
summary:
Background: 

So-called Medical Child Abuse is a specific form of child endangerment in which caregivers (in most cases, the parents) exaggerate, feign or actively induce symptoms of illness in the child. As a result, the healthcare system is instrumentalized for examinations, diagnoses, and treatments for which there is objectively no clinical necessity. This also generally means that, in this form of physical and emotional violence - unlike other forms of violence - professionals become “unwitting perpetrators” of the abuse, as the caregivers exploit the medical system for diagnostic and/or therapeutic purposes. Until now, the term “Munchausen by proxy syndrome” has often been used to describe this behavior. However, as part of professional development, the protection of the child and the actual physical and emotional harm are increasingly becoming the focus of professional discussion. Since it often takes months or even years for this abuse to be recognized, it is crucial that professionals are able to act early and decisively. In Germany, however, there is currently no data on how well-known this issue is in practice and what prevents professionals from intervening when abuse is suspected.

Research Question: 

Since this is primarily an exploratory project, the overarching goal is to conduct a systematic assessment of the implementation and practical relevance of the child-centered Medical Child Abuse concept in the interprofessional field (medicine, youth welfare, education) in Germany. A key part of the study’s objective is to assess professionals’ prior exposure to this issue in practice. We also aim to determine how well-versed professionals in the healthcare of minors and youth welfare (particularly youth welfare offices) are with the topic of Medical Child Abuse. We would like to learn how understandable and helpful they find the new technical term in contrast to Münchhausen by Proxy syndrome, and how confident they feel regarding case management when they have a corresponding suspicion regarding a child. Another focus is on identifying barriers: We want to understand which problems specific to Medical Child Abuse hinder swift action to protect the child.

Methods:

To answer these questions, we are conducting a nationwide survey using an online questionnaire. Professionals from relevant fields who work with children and adolescents are eligible to participate. Participation in the survey is voluntary and completely anonymous, so that no conclusions can be drawn about individual participants or their places of employment. Completing the questionnaire takes about 10 to 15 minutes. During the survey, participants will receive information on the topic as well as a brief real-life example to help them form their opinions. The results will be used exclusively for scientific purposes to further improve child protection in Germany.
